display_title: Nvidia Raises Shield TV Pro Price
display_title_he: אנבידיה מעלה את מחיר מכשיר הסטרימינג שלה
short_summary: Nvidia has increased the price of its seven-year-old Shield TV Pro streaming box by $100 due to rising component costs and a global memory shortage.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.title: Nvidia’s Shield TV Pro just got a $100 price hike

sources.name: Wired
sources.title: The Nvidia Shield TV Is 7 Years Old. It Just Got a $100 Price Hike

paragraphs: Technology supply chains are facing major changes due to the era of generative AI. According to recent reports, devices that rely on memory and storage are getting more expensive. Even older technology is subject to this trend, as seen with a popular media streaming device.

Nvidia has announced a $100 price increase for the Shield TV Pro. When the device originally launched nearly seven years ago, it sold for $199.99. However, starting on October 2nd, the price went up to $299.99. According to tech sources, this change is a direct result of the increased cost of components, particularly memory, across the entire industry.

At the same time, Nvidia has stopped production of the standard, cheaper version of the Shield TV, which previously cost $149.99. Moving forward, the company is focusing its manufacturing efforts exclusively on the Pro option. While cheaper competing streaming devices exist on the market, the Shield TV Pro continues to sell at its new higher price.

Industry experts note that high demand for artificial intelligence hardware, including AI chips and graphics processing units, has contributed to these dramatic price increases. Although the price hike may reduce consumer demand for the streaming box, Nvidia remains a dominant and highly valuable player in the global AI race.

facts.fact: Nvidia increased the price of the Shield TV Pro streaming box by $100, raising it from $199.99 to $299.99 starting October 2, 2026.
The price increase is due to a global memory shortage and rising component costs driven by the generative AI boom.
Nvidia has discontinued the standard, cheaper non-Pro version of the Shield TV, focusing production solely on the Pro model.
Nvidia dominates the AI hardware market with its GPUs and AI accelerators, which has contributed to high component costs across the tech industry.
